author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri. (A Tanna of the Mishnah.) Hyman writes that he was a great man of the generation in the academy of Yavneh. From whom he received his Torah we find in [Bava Kamma 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.70a.16-70b.3), where Rabbi Yose said: “When Abba Chalafta went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri to study Torah — and some say Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri to Abba Chalafta”; thus they were in doubt who was the teacher and who the student. But in the Tosefta we find several times the latter wording,

as in [Tosefta Maaser Sheni, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Maaser_Sheni.1.13): Rabbi Yose recounts that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri came to [Abba] Chalafta and asked about the safflower cake. Chalafta’s reply leads to Nuri’s response, “I too say so, but Akiva …” There, [Bava Batra, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Bava_Batra.2.4): Rabbi Yose again recounts Nuri’s visit to Abba Chalafta. The question begins, “One who took possession …,” and Nuri agrees with Chalafta’s answer before giving Akiva’s dissent. So it is there, [Ohalot, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Oholot.5.7), and Kelim 11:4.[^9] Hyman argues that reason supports this, for Rabbi Chalafta lived in Temple times

and still knew Rabban Gamliel the Elder, as Hyman reads [Shabbat 115a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.115a.7). Hyman places Chalafta near the generation indicated by the abbreviation [רי״בנ in the supplied Hebrew], and also in Rabban Gamliel’s generation. He places Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in the generation of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, as he will explain. Likewise we find that he spoke in the name of Rabbi Eliezer the Great, as in [Kiddushin 39a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39a.4), Tosefta Kelim, Bava Kamma, chapter 6, and Torat Kohanim, Shemini, chapter 4, 130: “Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said: I said to Rabbi Eliezer: If tents saved,” etc.

Some wish to say that he was Rabban Gamliel’s student, and bring proof from [Arakhin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.7), where Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said: “I call heaven and earth to witness against me that Akiva was flogged many times because I complained about him before Rabban Gamliel Berabbi.” Hyman replies that there is no proof from this that he was his student; rather, since Rabban Gamliel was the Patriarch and conducted his patriarchate with a high hand, all the sages of the generation were subordinate to him, as we will explain further.

He studied Torah in the greatest poverty, as stated explicitly in the Jerusalem Talmud, [beginning of Peah, chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.8.1.2): he would go out with the last gleaners and bring his livelihood for the whole year. Hyman cites [Sifrei Devarim 16:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.16.3) for the appointment of the two sages. In his account, when Rabbi Yehoshua was with Rabban Gamliel on a ship, Rabban Gamliel said to him: “You have so much [wisdom], and you go up on a ship?” Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: “Rather than wondering at me, wonder at two students you have on land, Rabbi Elazar Chisma

and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, who know how to calculate how many drops there are in the sea, and they have no bread to eat and no garment to wear.” He set his mind to seat them at the head, and when he went up [to land] he appointed them to some office. In [Horayot 10a:19-21](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.10a.19-21) Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada is, Hyman argues, cited in error; he writes: We have already explained in his entry that Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada was already the elder of the generation in Temple times, and it should read as in the Sifrei. Likewise what Rabbi Yehoshua said of them, “two

students you have” — this too is because all were subordinate to him; but in truth all were great men of the generation, as in [Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Rosh_Hashanah.2.8): an incident in which two came and said, “We saw it in the morning in the east and in the evening in the west.” Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said: “They are false witnesses.” When they came to Yavneh, Rabban Gamliel accepted them. Likewise he was like a colleague of Rabbi Yehoshua, as in [Eruvin 41a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.41a.6): after Rabban Gamliel’s death, Rabbi

Yehoshua came in to annul Rabban Gamliel’s words. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood on his feet and said: “I see that the body follows the head … Yehoshua, we do not listen to you.” In Ohalot 14:3 he disagrees with Rabbi Yehoshua. And what we find in Eruvin 10b, where Rabbi Yochanan said to Resh Lakish, “The incident was not so, for Rabbi Yehoshua went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri to study Torah … and addressed him as ‘Rabbi’” — Hyman calls this a scribal error and says it should read Rabbi Yehoshua ben

Korcha, and so it is stated explicitly in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 4:2 and Sukkah 1:4, and so is Rabbeinu Chananel’s reading. Hyman finds it very hard to understand [Tosafot on Nazir 65a:8:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Nazir.65a.8.2), who identify the Rabbi Yochanan who spoke in Ben Azzai’s name as Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri. His great and beloved colleague was Rabbi Akiva, as in [Arakhin 16b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.7), where Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said: “Many times Akiva was flogged through me … and all the more I increased his affection [for me].”[^10]

Most of his disputes in the Mishnah were with Rabbi Akiva, several times face to face, as in Rosh Hashanah 4:5, the end of Eduyot, chapter 2, Bekhorot 6:6, Temurah, beginning of chapter 1, Kelim 17:5, 17:6 and 30:2, Ohalot 2:7, Negaim, beginning of chapter 10, and 14:10, and Uktzin 3:5 and 3:6. Likewise in the Gemara, in baraitot, they disagree face to face, as in Pesachim 32, Gittin 89 and Bekhorot 40.

In [Yoma 38a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.38a.15) Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri relates: “Once I found an old man with a scroll of spices in his hand … When I came and told my words before Rabbi Akiva,” etc. In Tosefta Kelim, Bava Batra, beginning of chapter 2: “Rabbi Yose said: An incident with four elders who were sitting with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah in secret (חרש) in Tzippori: Rabbi Chutzpit the meturgeman, Rabbi Yeshevav, Rabbi Chalafta and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.” Zuckermandel’s Tosefta reads “Rabbi Yehoshua said,” and Hyman asserts that he is undoubtedly

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha; and Hyman considers Rabbi Shimshon’s text there to contain a scribal error. His halakhot in the Mishnah: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri is mentioned thirty-six times in the Mishnah, and his well-known halakhot are these: “The liver renders forbidden but is not rendered forbidden, because it emits and does not absorb,” Terumot 10:1. “The other species combine with one another,” Challah 4:2.

“One who slept on the road — he has two thousand cubits in every direction” (and from this, that ownerless objects acquire a Shabbat residence), and Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with him, Eruvin 4:5. “What do the mice care? Does it not eat whether from much or from little?” Bava Metzia 3:7.

“Eight creeping things have skins,” Chullin 9:2. “One who has relations with his mother-in-law is liable three [times] for her,” Keritot 3:6. “A bone the size of a barley grain that split is pure,” Ohalot 2:7. “A hailstone is like water” (regarding a mikveh), Mikvaot, beginning of chapter 6.

“All follows the appearance,” there, 5. In the Gemara, in a baraita, Shabbat 26: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood on his feet (against Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Yishmael) and said: “What shall the people of Babylonia do, who have no sesame oil?” [Pesachim 114b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.114b.9): “Rice is a kind of grain.” In [Sanhedrin 84a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.84a.14): “A non-Kohen who served in the Temple — by strangulation.” His fixed place: Hyman writes that although he undoubtedly took a great part

in the academy of Yavneh, as we brought above, his private residence was in the town of Ginnegar, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 4:5 and 6:4: an incident in which Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in Ginnegar. Sukkah 1:1 reads “to Genina,” and Eruvin 1:9 “to Gennegar.” In Kilayim 6:4 we find that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri burned the kilayim of the vineyard in Ginnegar. The view of Mavo HaMishnah, p. 125, is that his place

was in Beit She’arim, as we find in Tosefta Terumot, chapter 7: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka said: An incident in which Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka (my father) went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in Beit She’arim.” In the Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot, chapter 8, end of halakhah 3, it is the reverse, that he said: “An incident in which Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri went down to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, my father, in Beit Sharayin.” The Tosefta reading seems more likely to Hyman, for so we find

in Tosefta Sukkah, beginning of chapter 2: “Rabbi said: Once we were coming, I and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok, to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in Beit She’arim.” But Hyman calls this a scribal error and says it should read “Berabbi said,” according to the Gra’s reading, referring to Rabbi Yose above, whom they called Rabbi Yose Berabbi; for Rabbi did not see Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri. We find that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok disagrees with him in Niddah 46b. Of those who speak in his name we find Kiddushin 38b

and Menachot 35b, that Rabbi Yose HaGelili received from him a halakhah that he had heard from Rabbi Eliezer the Great. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha received much from him, as cited above. Likewise Hyman identifies Rabbi Yose as his distinguished student, who always related incidents he had seen of him, as in Bekhorot 1:10: “Rabbi Yose said: An incident with a girl … Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said: If the majority,” etc. Likewise Tosefta Sheviit, chapter 6:

“Rabbi Yose said: An incident in which they sowed … and the case came before Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri”; there, Megillah, chapter 2: “Rabbi Yose said: An incident with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, who read it (the Megillah) in Tzippori at night. They said to him: A time of danger is no proof” (Hyman asserts that this was undoubtedly when they hid with Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, as cited in Tosefta Kelim, Bava Batra, beginning of chapter 2). Likewise there, Yevamot, chapter 6. Likewise Rabbi Yose spoke in his name, Kelim, Bava Batra, chapter 7, and in Torat Kohanim, Shemini, chapter 7, Rabbi Yose answered

Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri. Likewise we find Chilfa bar Agra speaking in his name, as in [Shabbat 105b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.105b.8). Seder HaDorot cites that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai studied with him, citing Eruvin, chapter 1, but Hyman reports finding this neither there nor anywhere else. In aggadah only his precious saying remains to us, [Shabbat 105b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.105b.8), where he said: “One who tears his garments in his anger, breaks his vessels in his anger, or scatters his money

in his anger — let him be in your eyes like an idolater.” In Eduyot 2:10 he said: “The judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is from Passover until Shavuot.” He was praised by Issi ben Yehudah as “a peddlers’ basket,” and in Avot deRabbi Natan, chapter 18, as “a basket of halakhot.” Hyman thinks he apparently died before the destruction of Betar, as is implied in [Yevamot 15a:1-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.15a.1-3), where he said: “Come, let us make an enactment

for the rival wives” — they did not manage to finish the matter before the times turned troubled. And what they said there, “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to him: What shall we do with the earlier rival wives?” is, Hyman argues, a scribal error; it should read, as cited in Tosefta Yevamot, chapter 1, “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said.” In Avot deRabbi Natan, end of chapter 40, they said: “One who sees Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri in a dream may hope for fear of sin.”

In Arakhin 16b the proverb about rebuking a wise man supports reading the increase as Akiva’s affection for the speaker. The consulted text names Rabban Shimon Beribbi where Hyman has Rabban Gamliel. Bava Kamma 70a–b gives both directions of the visit between Chalafta and Yohanan, while the consulted Tosefta parallels have Yohanan visit Chalafta. These reports leave their broader teacher–student relationship open.

The consulted Eruvin 11b has Rabbi Yehoshua without a patronymic. The field episodes in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 4:2, Sukkah 1:1 and Eruvin 1:9 name Yehoshua ben Korcha and vary in the place name. Hyman’s proposed correction and his report of Rabbeinu Chananel’s reading belong to his account. The consulted Horayot 10a names Yohanan ben Gudgeda in the ship dialogue, while the consulted Sifrei Devarim 16 names Yohanan ben Nuri alongside Elazar Chasma in the appointment episode. The consulted Tosefta Sukkah 2 includes “Rabbi said” in brackets. The Gra reading is reported by Hyman. The consulted Terumot parallels reverse the direction of the visit. Hyman’s preference is his own inference.

The consulted Shabbat 26a says the Babylonians had only sesame oil. Hyman’s supplied wording says they had no sesame oil. The consulted Mikvaot 7:1 attributes “a hailstone is like water” to Yohanan ben Nuri. This is a close parallel to the supplied stone designation, which remains uncertain. The appearance rule occurs at Mikvaot 7:5 in the consulted edition. The liver statement appears at Terumot 10:11, the split bone at Oholot 2:7, and the girl and majority episode at Ketubot 1:10. The supplied citations are retained. The consulted Pesachim 35a and Sanhedrin 84a contain the cited positions on rice and strangulation. The source’s Sheviit incident word remains unresolved.

The consulted Yevamot 14b–15a contains the proposal and direct reply. Tosefta Yevamot 1 has Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s question without “to him,” as Hyman recommends. The proposal and the report that times turned troubled leave his inference about Betar open. Hyman’s census of Mishnah mentions, claims about teaching and residence, and reports about printed readings are retained as his. The consulted texts corroborate individual passages and leave the uncollated editions open.

Hyman’s printed page 683 has חלת הריע and brackets the word Abba, as in the supplied Hebrew. The consulted Tosefta Maaser Sheni 1:13 has חלות חריע and names Chalafta without Abba. Tosefta Kifshutah discusses הריע as a spelling of חריע and treats the item as a safflower cake. It also notes that the texts it cites call him Rabbi Chalafta.

The first generation abbreviation on printed page 683 is unclear in the scan. Its last letter resembles a vav, while the supplied Hebrew gives רי״בנ and the second occurrence in print ends in nun. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai has been proposed from the context. In Shabbat 115a Chalafta visits the younger Rabban Gamliel, and the recollection concerns the Elder. The Hebrew leaves the speaker of the recollection unnamed, and the consulted Davidson English assigns it to Yochanan HaNazuf. Rashi distinguishes the two Gamliels and places the younger one in Chalafta’s generation. Hyman’s chronology remains his reading.

Printed page 684 cites Ohalot 2:7 and has אבן הברד, “a hailstone,” beside supplied Ohalot 3:6 and אבן הכבד. The consulted Mishnah Oholot 2:7 gives the split bone ruling. Hyman cites the beginning of Mikvaot chapter 6; the named hailstone ruling is at Mikvaot 7:1 in the consulted edition.

Printed page 684 cites Pesachim 114b and Sanhedrin 84a beside supplied 104b and 85a. The consulted Pesachim 114b quotes Nuri’s rice ruling in a discussion in which Rav Ashi rejects reliance on it; it also appears at 35a. The consulted Sanhedrin 84a contrasts Nuri’s strangulation ruling with Akiva’s stoning ruling. On sesame oil, the supplied and printed wording says “no sesame oil,” while the consulted Shabbat 26a says “only sesame oil.”

Hyman’s printed page 685 cites Tosefta Sheviit chapter 6 and has שורעו, as in the supplied Hebrew. In the consulted Tosefta Sheviit 4:7 the word is שזרעו. Rabbi Yose reports that onions were planted in a large vineyard in Tzippori and that barley was sown there after the sabbatical year. Workers gathered greens, and the matter came before Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, whose ruling depended on comparable produce having grown. Hyman quotes the incident in abbreviated form.

Printed page 685 has פ״יח (chapter 18), while the supplied Hebrew has פ״ח (chapter 8). The consulted Vilna text of Avot deRabbi Natan 18 calls Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri a “basket of halakhot,” including in its list of Issi’s epithets. In that chapter the “peddlers’ basket” description is given to Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah. Hyman’s separate attribution is retained in the translation.

[Bava Kamma 70a–70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.70a.16-70b.3) preserves both directions for the study visit. The linked Tosefta examples have Nuri visiting Chalafta, but they do not call either visitor the other’s teacher in those accounts. [Seder HaDorot 1814](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1814&lang=en) likewise reports both possibilities. Hyman argues for the direction found in the Tosefta.

[Horayot 10a:19-21](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.10a.19-21) names Yochanan ben Gudgeda in the ship story. Rabban Gamliel’s speech on the appointment continues at [Horayot 10b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.10b.1). [Sifrei Devarim 16:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.16.3) names Yochanan ben Nuri and Elazar Chisma in the appointment story. Hyman proposes reading Nuri in the Bavli. The field incident cited as Eruvin 10b appears at [Eruvin 11b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.5), which gives Yehoshua without a patronymic. At [Nazir 65a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.65a.10), Rabbi Yochanan speaks in Ben Azzai’s name; [Tosafot on Nazir 65a:8:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Nazir.65a.8.2) identifies him as Nuri. The examined [Niddah 47a:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.47a.18) gives Elazar ben Tzadok and Yochanan ben Beroka, leaving Hyman’s Niddah 46b attribution to Nuri unresolved. [Kiddushin 39a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.39a.4) has Rabbi Yose HaGelili report in Nuri’s name a ruling Nuri attributes to Rabbi Eliezer the Great. [Menachot 38b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.38b.13) has Rabbi Yose HaGelili report a different ruling in Nuri’s name; its chain stops with Nuri. The proposal concerning rival wives begins at [Yevamot 14b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.14b.16) and continues at [Yevamot 15a:1-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.15a.1-3).
